comment: The draft explicitly warns that centralized interoperability layers risk "concentration of control, single points of failure and procurement bottlenecks" (p.72) but gives no criteria for when a country should choose centralised vs. federated vs. hybrid. Based on our field experience, the decision factors (national IT capacity, existing platform landscape, donor funding structure, political economy) actually driving this choice are pragmatic. The architecture is rarely chosen in advance, but accrues over time via installed base, funding availability, and IT capacity at MoH to manage ETL middleware. Thus the guidance on interoperability layer to choose should be studied in more detail.

reviewer.name: Brian O'Donnell (on behalf of HISP-UiO)
reviewer.organisation: HISP Centre at University of Oslo
